This is a fantastic game. I think it's the strongest in their entire series. You'll find everything you want in Civil War, real-time strategy. The battles are smooth, and the army customization really adds to the flavor of the game. The only thing I would say is perhaps a weakness is the fact that when you win battles, it doesn't really affect your campaign in the sense that you can maneuver to different battles. For example, if you win Gettysburg as the Confederacy, you still just fight the next battle. Or if you really smash the Confederacy as the Union, you're still kind of stuck to the historical campaign. You just start each battle stronger. And it can actually get to the point where you've kneecapped the enemy army so badly that it becomes kind of a wash-over, but it's still a very fun game. Its the real inheritor of Sid Meyers original Gettysburg. 
So I would say if you love maneuvering columns of Civil War infantry around, as well as managing cavalry that can dismount and a variety of artillery, you'll like this game. Play style is basically capture the flag, but like so many games in this genre, you're really trying to surround and destroy your enemy in encirclement battles where massed rifle fire makes the difference. And you can upgrade units with everything from Mexican-American War-style rifles all the way through state-of-the-art Civil War guns, including the Henry rifle and Sharps carbine, things like that. Cavalry can be equipped as melee or dismounted specialists. There's also a variety of artillery, so you can customize your artillery force, it's quite fun.  Key to the game is the Barracks mode between main battles and skirmishes. These skirmishes serve as preliminary battles before major campaign battles like Antietam or Gettysburg. They give you an opportunity to win, to collect money and resources to optimize your army in order to win the big multi stage campaign battles. The barracks are important because that's where you enhance your character (general characteristics like politics medicine and logistics)  create new divisions to increase the size of your army, and add customizable attributes to your generals and individual divisions so you can take them from, essentially, greenhorn militiamen with antique 1840s weapons to crack infantry armed with state-of-the-art 1863 weapons after a few campaigns. But resource management is critical in this game, and it's quite fun to do. The decisions you make in the barracks absolutely affect your potential to win the battles. For example, you can choose to reinforce a division with veteran troops and expensive weapons, but if you do that, it will come at the cost of massing large formations. And so you'll have these elite crack units that are capable of holding their own until attrition breaks them if you prefer that, and you're a good player, that will work. But for the same money, you could have bought four low-quality divisions with four times as many soldiers on the field maneuvering. So it's up to you. And that part of the resource management is actually a lot of fun pre-battle to see if you can tune the army just right for the coming challenges.

J’ai passé un temps monstrueux sur ce jeu. Avec plus de 2 700 heures dessus, autant dire qu’il m’a marqué. Et visiblement, je suis loin d’être le seul : certains dépassent les 3 000 heures de jeu, et voir autant de joueurs avec plusieurs centaines d’heures au compteur montre bien que le titre a quelque chose de spécial.

Je ne vais pas revenir en détail sur le gameplay, beaucoup l’ont déjà fait avant moi. Mais au fond, le principe est simple : avancer, tenir une ligne, grignoter du terrain. Et finalement, c’est une représentation assez brute de ce qu’est une guerre.

Évidemment, le jeu n’est pas parfait. On pourrait facilement dresser une longue liste de défauts. Mais malgré ça, il réussit l’essentiel : il est prenant. Il crée cette tension permanente où l’on se surprend à crier mentalement : « Tenez la ligne ! », « Avancez ! », « Poussez-les ! ».

Beaucoup le comparent à un TW, mais sans l’aspect stratégique. Personnellement, en tant qu’ancien grand amateur des TW, je trouve aujourd’hui leurs batailles assez fades. Visuellement, c’est superbe, oui, mais tactiquement, notamment à cause de l’IA, je m'ennuie depuis que j'ai joué à UG : Civil War.

Et c’est justement là que vient mon incompréhension.
Voilà un studio qui :
1. a réussi à créer un concept original qui fonctionne réellement ;
2. a trouvé une communauté fidèle et passionnée ;
3. disposait déjà d’une base solide pour continuer à développer cette licence et ce concept.

Et pourtant, au lieu d’exploiter ce qui faisait leur force, ils ont voulu partir dans tous les sens : ajouter des batailles navales parce que c’est leur spécialité, miser sur la 3D, injecter davantage de stratégie… Bref, essayer de se rapprocher des TW. Sauf qu’au final, ça donnait surtout une version moins bonne.

Alors franchement, pourquoi ne pas avoir simplement développé ce qui marchait ?

過去にプレイしたリアルタイム性のウォーシミュレーションゲームは信長の野望・嵐世記以降、大戦略４・６、Victoriaシリーズなどがあり、本作は19世紀半ばの奴隷制解放をめぐる南北戦争を再現している。
初戦が伏兵に敵味方双方の増援、市街戦、戦車列車など、プレイヤーによって挫折するかもしれないほどCOMはえぐい攻撃をしてくる。ゆえに、裏をかいて森を抜けて背後を突くなり、二重歩兵連隊を向かわせて前面が盾になっている間に後ろの隊に突撃をかけて潰走させるなり、三方面から囲んで投降させるなり、多様な戦略が楽しめるゲームである。

マップをクリアするたびに報酬がもらえ、自軍を補充・強化できることもいいし、キャリアによって軍の規模の維持重視か質向上重視かの判断ができるところもよい。戦果を挙げれば追加資金なり強力な武器なりもらえるので、徐々に数万人を動かせる将軍気分を味わえる。鍛え上げた軍団で敵軍を包囲・殲滅・投降させた際はSっ気が炸裂するし、逆に人数で上回っているのに押されるときはFワードを口走るしw

唯一残念なのが、自軍を遠く離れた敵（補給部隊・指揮官・散兵等）に攻撃指示を出すと、榴弾砲の攻撃範囲よりもはるか先なのに察知して逃げ出す点。せっかく索敵要素を持っているのだから、敵側の索敵範囲外での即察知はおかしい。ま、それを利用して、自軍に対峙する散兵や騎兵、指揮官を散兵や騎兵で狙わせるとすぐに逃げてくれるので、歩兵の士気が重層的に削られて持久戦が厳しい場合に使える戦術にもなっているのだが。

局地戦は時に編成仕立てたばかりの新兵部隊の鍛錬にして小銭を稼ぎ、大戦は全軍の総力を挙げて敵軍を潰走させ、包囲・殲滅を目指し大金を得る。今は7～8万人規模と、徐々に発展していく自軍が頼もしく見えてきたら、戦争終結の時も近づくのだろう。

Worth a try. Its a bit of a slog, points for realism I guess. Given the general draught of decent RTS games this does stand out. I have mostly enjoyed it but I'm on the fence about pushing through to finish the campaigns as is starts to feel grindy.

I think they nailed the scale pretty well, Pitched battles of 50-100k soldiers feel appropriately large and chaotic. Smaller scale battles with deployment limits also generally work but with larger brigades it can feel like there isn't enough space on the map to actually use even the limited numbers they let you bring.

Some very annoying things:
Enemy veteran units have absurd morale, if a general is standing near them they won't break even at high casualties or being rear and side flanked, they will also reform in seconds one broken, this heavily contributes to the grind.
The bigger battles are broken into sections that add, remove, or adjust map boundaries at different stages. Sometimes this is executed really well, other times a handful of brigades you thought were watching a flank are suddenly in direct contact of 4x their number with a line a cannons behind them.
The game doesn't clearly communicate that need to spend your career points on unlocking larger army sizes by certain points of the campaign and you can end up in unwinnable battles because you can't bring enough soldiers.

So, the battles themselves are generally enjoyable.  The AI sometimes shows some skill.  The battle clock is sometimes short making any significant maneuver problematic.  Some of the battles have victory conditions that are absurd.  Nevertheless, the battles are fun.  

The campaign is crap.  All is well if you win.  End in a draw (or most certainly a loss) in any significant battle and the game will put you into a death spiral: the campaign is over - you will be defeated.  It does not matter if you crushed the enemy in every battle beforehand.  With a draw (or loss) the game mechanics stack the enemy strength up against you in a very significant way.  Your next battle will require you to achieve every victory condition with insufficient combat power to do it.  Eventually, the enemy will get bigger and bigger and you have no chance.  This mechanic is just plain lazy on the part of the developers.  

Buy it on sale, it still has some value - just don't expect much from a campaign.
